name: Substantiv
subtitle: Nouns: en/ett, definite forms and plural Groups 1–5

ruleCards.title: En or ett?
ruleCards.rule: Every noun is an en-word or an ett-word. About three in four are en-words. There is no reliable rule, so learn the article with the word.
ruleCards.watch: Words for people are almost always en-words: en lärare, en man, en kvinna. But: ett barn.

ruleCards.title: The definite form
ruleCards.rule: Swedish puts “the” at the end of the word. En-words add -en or -n, ett-words add -et or -t.
ruleCards.watch: Words ending in -el and -er often just add -n: nyckel → nyckeln, syster → systern.

ruleCards.title: Group 1: the -or house
ruleCards.rule: En-words that end in -a drop the a and add -or.
ruleCards.watch: A few words without -a also take -or: en ros → rosor.

ruleCards.title: Group 2: the -ar house
ruleCards.rule: Short concrete en-words, en-words with an e in one of the last two letters, and -ing words.
ruleCards.watch: The last e often disappears: fågel → fåglar, syster → systrar.

ruleCards.title: Group 3: the -er and -r house
ruleCards.rule: Long en-words, words from other languages and words stressed on the last syllable add -er. En-words ending in a vowel other than a add only -r.
ruleCards.watch: Some short words change their vowel: bok → böcker, stad → städer, hand → händer, natt → nätter.

ruleCards.title: Group 3 exceptions
ruleCards.rule: These look like short Group 2 words, but they take -er. Learn them by heart.
ruleCards.watch: Vän doubles the n: vännen, vänner, vännerna.

ruleCards.title: Group 4: the -n house
ruleCards.rule: Ett-words that end in a vowel add -n.
ruleCards.watch: Irregular: ett öga → ögon, ett öra → öron.

ruleCards.title: Group 5: the no-ending house
ruleCards.rule: Ett-words that end in a consonant, and en-words for people ending in -are or -er, look the same in the plural.

ruleCards.title: The definite plural
ruleCards.rule: Start from the plural. Groups 1–3 add -na, Group 4 adds -a, Group 5 ett-words add -en.
ruleCards.watch: En-words ending in -are drop the e: lärare → lärarna. Rum doubles the m: rummen.
